issues: [Med/Repetition & monotony] Over-repetition of Maya explicitly stating she is nervous. — Maya's nerves are asserted in three consecutive scenes: 'jeg er også lidt nervøs' (Scene 1), 'Jeg var lidt nervøs' (Scene 2), and 'Jeg kiggede nervøst' (Scene 3). Asserting the exact same emotional state explicitly across consecutive scenes creates a monotonous emotional loop.

[Med/Repetition & monotony] Repetitive use of 'aldrig/ikke [gjort noget] før', including an exact duplicate line. — The exact sentence 'Jeg har aldrig arbejdet på/i en café før' is used in both Scene 1 and Scene 4, making it feel like a jarring reset. Additionally, Scenes 2 and 5 use the exact same template ('Jeg har aldrig lavet kaffe... før', 'Jeg havde ikke serveret en gingerbeer før'), turning this into an overused refrain.

[Low/Repetition & monotony] Explicitly restating nervousness. — Scenes 1, 2, and 3 all explicitly state the exact emotion 'nervøs' ('lidt nervøs', 'lidt nervøs', 'nervøst'). While it makes sense for her first shift, asserting it three scenes in a row is slightly monotonous.

[Low/Repetition & monotony] Repeated use of the emotion/word 'nervøs' in the first three scenes. — Maya mentions being 'lidt nervøs' in Scene 1, 'lidt nervøs' again in Scene 2, and looking 'nervøst' in Scene 3. Varying the way she expresses her beginner's apprehension would make the emotional arc feel more dynamic.

[High/Repetition & monotony] Verbatim repetition of a line from Scene 1. — Maya says 'Jeg har aldrig arbejdet i en café før' (I have never worked in a café before). She already said this exact phrase in Scene 1. Repeating it in Scene 4 reads like an accidental copy-paste and creates jarring narrative amnesia (furthermore, using it to contrast with 'learning to cut bread in half quickly' feels slightly absurd).

[High/Cross-scene continuity & consistency] Contradiction regarding the volume of coffee made. — In Scene 3, Maya serves her 'very first coffee' and fulfills her 'first order'. Scene 4 happens 'shortly after' and introduces 'the next order', but Maya then states 'I have already made a lot of coffee today.' It is logically impossible for her to have made a lot of coffee between her first and second order of the day.

[Low/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Redundant narrative premise. — Maya states 'I have never worked in a café before' in Scene 4, which she already explicitly stated in Scene 1. Since both scenes take place during the exact same morning shift, repeating the premise to the listener feels a bit repetitive, even for a language course.

[Med/Repetition & monotony] Repeated line: 'Jeg har aldrig arbejdet i en café før.' — This exact sentiment and phrasing was already established in Scene 1. Repeating it in Scene 4 feels like a reset, and it creates a clunky transition into 'But I have learned to cut the bread in half quickly'.

[Med/Naive whole-week listener (no checklist)] Abrupt repetition of exposition mid-action: 'Jeg har aldrig arbejdet i en café før.' — Maya already established this exact fact in Scene 1. Repeating it as an independent thought right in the middle of slicing a sourdough bun breaks the narrative flow and makes the narrator sound like she has amnesia.
